newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish audit office sees lower deficit, borrowing.
newsitem.headline: Swedish audit office sees lower deficit, borrowing.

text.p: Sweden's National Audit Office on Thursday lowered its forecasts for the 1995/96 18-month fiscal period budget deficit to 147 billion crowns from an earlier forecast of 159 billion crowns.
The office also lowered its forecast for national borrowing requirement in calendar 1996 to 31 billion crowns from 54 billion.
The audit office last released forecasts in August.
Releasing new figures for 1997 and 1998, the office said it saw the budget deficit in 1997 at 39 billion crowns.
Government income in 1998 was forecast at 650 billion crowns.
The office said government income in 1997, forecast at 625.2 billion crowns, would be boosted by the sale of the state's 34-percent holding in mortgage bank Stadshypotek.
However, the estimate did not include the proposed sale of the state's reamining interest in Nordbanken.
The audit office said its revision to the national borrowing requirement followed a similar lowering by the National Debt Office.
"The main reason for the change is the bigger repayment of loans," the audit office said in a statement.
Regarding the economy, the audit office forecasts 1997 gross domestic product growth of 2.7 percent and 2.4 percent in 1998 after increasing 1.5 percent this year.
It saw the consumer price index rising 0.8 percent in calendar 1996 but increasing 1.0 percent next year and 2.2 percent in 1998.
